claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and the children you're inquiring about.

**Could you please tell me the name and age of the first child you'd like me to assess?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 9 years old.

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation better.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to check a few more details about your residency status, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, an EU citizen, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful.

One more important question about your circumstances:

**Are you currently working or receiving any income? If so, what is the approximate total amount you earn or receive per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do work, yes. I earn around £35,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Now let me gather the specific eligibility rules to make sure I assess your situation correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I have reviewed all the eligibility rules for Child Benefit. Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Alex.

**Summary of your situation:**
- You are a British citizen living in the UK ✓
- Alex is 9 years old (under 16) ✓
- Alex lives with you ✓
- You earn £35,000 per year

According to the eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You meet these criteria as you live with Alex and are responsible for them.

Your income of £35,000 does not exceed the £60,000 threshold mentioned for the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, so there are no income-related barriers to your eligibility.

Based on all the information gathered, I can now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

You meet all the necessary criteria:
- Alex is under 16 and lives with you
- You are responsible for Alex
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Your income does not exceed the threshold for the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can now proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!
